chunks: As for the right of the one who does a kindly act toward you,

is that you thank him and mention his kindness; you spread good words about him, and you sincerely supplicate for him between you and God Almighty. For if you do that, you have thanked him secretly and openly. Then, if you are able to repay him one day, you repay him.

key_terms.ذِي الْمَعْرُوفِ: The one who does a kindly act or bestows a favor

ai.seo_question: What are the specific duties of a person who receives a favor according to Shia Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin distinguishes between the social obligation of public praise (nashr al-maqala al-husna) and the spiritual act of private supplication (du'a), framing gratitude as a holistic duty encompassing both word and deed. This dual approach reflects the Shia emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) in interpersonal relations, ensuring that thanks are not merely performative but rooted in genuine appreciation. The instruction to repay if capable underscores the reciprocal nature of social bonds in Islamic ethics, moving beyond mere politeness to active reciprocity.

en.william-c-chittick: The right of him who does a kindly act (dhu l-ma'ruf) toward you is that you thank him and mention his kindness; you reward him with beautiful words and you supplicate for him sincerely in that which is between you and God.
If you do that, you have thanked him secretly and openly. Then, if you are able to repay him one day, you repay him.
